  "text": "At morning Tobias came by the church road with a loaf under his coat. He had bought two without asking himself why.

The house stood above the dune. Its door was shut. Along the path the eleven posts held their wire, and on the third a bead of water trembled without falling.

He knocked with the hand that held no bread.

There was nothing improper in the silence. Maren might have gone to the shop. She might have been upstairs, moving carefully on the knee that troubled her in wet weather. He waited long enough to allow for both.

Then he tried the latch.

The front room was cold. The lamp stood unlit on the sill, its chipped side turned toward the glass. He put the loaf on the table. There was yesterday's cup, washed and upside down beside the sink.

He had meant to call her name. Inside the house it seemed a thing he ought to have asked permission to do.

Instead he straightened the rug with his boot. One corner had folded under, as it always did when someone came in from the passage.

At the door he stopped. Across the dry boards lay a narrow line of sand. It began at the window and ended at the chair where Maren's mother used to sit.

Tobias left the bread where it was.

Outside, he pulled the door until the latch caught. He tested it once, gently, with his thumb.

Then he took the church road home, carrying the other loaf in both hands.",
